name: Suvorexant
short: DORA with comparable OX1 and OX2 affinity.
mechanism: A reversible, competitive antagonist with **comparable affinity for OX1 and OX2**; blocks orexin’s stabilization of wakefulness so the patient sleeps. Orexin rising in the morning reverses the block.

sideEffects.e: No dependence, withdrawal, rebound, falls, amnesia or respiratory depression (compared with GABA-A PAMs)
sideEffects.via: Reduces arousal rather than enhancing GABA

sideEffects.e: Morning carryover in some patients (lower the dose)

name: Lemborexant
short: DORA with higher OX2 affinity and fast kinetics.
mechanism: A reversible DORA with **higher affinity for OX2 than OX1** and much **faster association/dissociation** at OX2, perhaps reversing faster as morning orexin rises.

sideEffects.e: No dependence, withdrawal, rebound, falls, amnesia or respiratory depression (compared with GABA-A PAMs)
sideEffects.via: Reduces arousal rather than enhancing GABA

sideEffects.e: Morning carryover in some patients (lower the dose)

name: Daridorexant
short: DORA in development at publication; later approved for insomnia.
mechanism: A dual orexin receptor antagonist mentioned in the book as in development.

updates.title: Approved for insomnia
updates.text: Approved by the FDA in January 2022 (25 and 50 mg) for adults with insomnia with difficulty in sleep onset and/or maintenance.

name: Ramelteon
mechanism: **MT1/MT2 agonist**; improves **sleep onset** (sometimes better after several days), not maintenance; short time above threshold.

name: Tasimelteon
short: MT1/MT2 agonist for non-24-hour sleep–wake disorder.
mechanism: A powerful **MT1/MT2 agonist**; MT2 action retrains the circadian clock.

name: Memantine
short: NMDA antagonist at NAM/Mg²⁺ sites; pro-cognitive in Alzheimer disease.
mechanism: An **antagonist** at the **NAM channel/Mg²⁺ sites** of NMDA glutamate receptors. Details in Chapter 12.

targets.note: Uncompetitive open-channel block at the Mg²⁺ site; low affinity

facts.text: Listed in Table 3-2 as the NMDA glutamate antagonist that is pro-cognitive in Alzheimer disease.

An **uncompetitive, open-channel** NMDA antagonist with low-to-moderate affinity, **voltage dependence** and fast on/off kinetics: blocks tonic excitotoxic glutamate but is expelled by phasic bursts, so learning continues and there are no psychotomimetic effects (“**artificial magnesium**”).
Usually given **with** a cholinesterase inhibitor for additive benefit; not effective (or tested) for agitation.

name: Donepezil
mechanism: A **reversible, long-acting, selective AChE inhibitor** with no BuChE inhibition. Raises ACh at surviving postsynaptic cholinergic receptors in cortex and hippocampus.

sideEffects.via: Peripheral AChE inhibition in the gut

facts.text: Easy to dose; side effects mostly **GI** and transient.

updates.title: A weekly donepezil patch
updates.text: **Adlarity** (donepezil transdermal system, once weekly) was approved in March 2022; it was later listed as discontinued.

name: Rivastigmine
short: Pseudoirreversible AChE and BuChE inhibitor; patch available.
mechanism: A **pseudoirreversible** (reverses over hours), intermediate-acting inhibitor of **AChE and BuChE**, possibly selective for cortical and hippocampal AChE. Glial BuChE inhibition may matter more as gliosis advances.

sideEffects.e: More GI effects orally than donepezil
sideEffects.via: PK profile; peripheral AChE and BuChE inhibition

facts.text: Comparable efficacy and safety to donepezil; the **transdermal patch** greatly reduces GI effects by lowering peaks. (The book also calls it “selective for AChE over BuChE”; it is a dual inhibitor.)

name: Galantamine
short: AChE inhibitor and nicotinic positive allosteric modulator.
mechanism: Inhibits **AChE** and is a **positive allosteric modulator** of nicotinic receptors, theoretically amplifying the extra ACh at nicotinic sites; clinical advantage unproven.

sideEffects.via: Peripheral AChE inhibition in the gut

name: Aducanumab
mechanism: Monoclonal antibody that binds aggregated **Aβ** and removes plaque.

sideEffects.e: ARIA-E (brain edema) and ARIA-H (microbleeds), rarely fatal
sideEffects.via: Amyloid removal from vessel walls; higher risk in APOE4 carriers

facts.text: Anti-amyloid antibodies are listed in Table 12-6 among disease-modifying strategies that had not shown clinical benefit when the book was written.

updates.title: Approved, then discontinued
updates.text: Accelerated approval on June 7, 2021 based on plaque reduction; Biogen discontinued it on January 31, 2024, citing reasons unrelated to safety or efficacy.

name: Lecanemab
short: Anti-Aβ protofibril antibody for early AD; IV or subcutaneous.
mechanism: Monoclonal antibody against soluble Aβ **protofibrils** and plaque; clears amyloid and modestly slows decline in early AD.
uses: **Early Alzheimer disease** (MCI or mild dementia with confirmed amyloid)

sideEffects.e: ARIA-E (brain edema) and ARIA-H (microbleeds), rarely fatal
sideEffects.via: Amyloid removal from vessel walls; higher risk in APOE4 carriers

facts.text: Anti-amyloid antibodies are listed in Table 12-6 among disease-modifying strategies that had not shown clinical benefit when the book was written.

updates.title: Traditional approval and new forms
updates.text: Accelerated approval January 6, 2023; traditional approval July 2023; IV maintenance dosing January 2025; subcutaneous autoinjector (Leqembi Iqlik) for maintenance August 2025 and for starting treatment July 2026. Boxed warning for ARIA; test APOE4 before treatment.

name: Donanemab
short: Anti-plaque antibody for early AD; can stop after plaque clearance.
mechanism: Monoclonal antibody against a modified form of Aβ in **deposited plaque**; treatment can stop once plaque is cleared.

sideEffects.e: ARIA-E (brain edema) and ARIA-H (microbleeds), rarely fatal
sideEffects.via: Amyloid removal from vessel walls; higher risk in APOE4 carriers

facts.text: Anti-amyloid antibodies are listed in Table 12-6 among disease-modifying strategies that had not shown clinical benefit when the book was written.

updates.title: Donanemab approved
updates.text: Approved July 2, 2024 for early symptomatic AD, IV every 4 weeks; boxed warning for ARIA; label updated with modified titration in July 2025.
